Mukkunnukaran Narayanan vs The Government Of Kerala on 26 September, 2025

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137867724/

 Judgment
1. The claimant in LAR No.26/2015 is the appellant.
As per the impugned judgment, a reference under Section 28A(3) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, at the instance of the claimant was rejected.

His other reference as LAR No.27/2015 under Section 28A(3) is allowed as per the impugned judgment fixing the land value at the rate of Rs.1,500/- per cent relying on Ext.A1 judgment of the same Court, which is modified by this Court in Ext.A2 judgment.
This Appeal is filed claiming fixation of land value at Rs.1,500/- per cent in LAR No.26/2015 also.
2. I heard the learned counsel for the appellant, Sri. V.N. Ramesan Nambisan and the learned Senior Government Pleader, Smt. Rekha C. Nair.

3. The contention of the learned counsel for the appellant is that the claim of the appellant on the basis of Exts.A1 and A2 was illegally rejected by the Reference Court, finding that there is no evidence that the property included in Exts.A1 and A2 and the acquired property LA.APP. NO. 238 OF 2019 2025:KER:72256 are comparable.

On the other hand, in LAR No.27/2015, the Court found that the property involved in Exts.A1 and A2 and the acquired property in LAR No.27/2015 are comparable since both the properties are situated in the same survey number, and hence, the land value at the rate of Rs.1,500/- per cent was given.

The learned counsel contended that in all these three cases, namely, LAR No.26/2015, LAR No.27/2015 and Ext.A1 L.A.R., the Land Acquisition Officer granted the same value, namely, Rs.1,15,200/- per hectare, equivalent to Rs.466/- per cent.

Hence, the claimant in the present case also is entitled to get fixation of land value at the rate of Rs.1,500/- per cent on the basis of Exts.A1 and A2, as all these properties are acquired as per the very same section 4(1) Notification dated 22.02.1983 for the very same purpose, namely, for the establishment of Ezhimala Naval Academy.

4. On the other hand, the learned Senior Government Pleader contended that in view of Section 28A of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, the evidence as to acquisition of properties as per the very same Section LA.APP. NO. 238 OF 2019 2025:KER:72256 4(1) Notification alone is not sufficient.
There should be evidence before the Court that both properties are comparable.

The appellant/claimant did not adduce any evidence to show that the property acquired from him is comparable to the property covered by Ext.A1 produced before the District Collector along with the Section 28A Application.
Hence, the Reference Court correctly answered the Reference, rejecting the claim, and the appeal is liable to be dismissed.
5. I have considered the rival contentions.
6. The property involved in LAR No.26/2015 is 0.3760 hectares of land in R.S. No.411/7 of Ramanthali Village.
The property involved in LAR No.27/2015 is 0.7514 hectares in R.S. No.309/1 of Ramanthali village.

Both these properties were acquired as per the very same Section 4(1)
Notification dated 22.02.1983.
In both cases, compensation was awarded, fixing land value at the rate of Rs.1,15,200/- per Hectare.

When the Reference Court passed Ext.A1 judgment in LAR No.120/1987, the claimant filed Applications LA.APP. NO. 238 OF 2019 2025:KER:72256 under Section 28A of the Land Acquisition Act for the determination of land value in accordance with Mukkunnukaran Narayanan vs The Government Of Kerala on 26 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137867724/

sentences.text: Ext.A1 judgment with respect to both acquisitions.
In Ext.A1 judgment, the land value fixed is Rs.2,47,000/- per hectare, equivalent to Rs.1,000/- per cent.
The property involved in Ext.A1 judgment also was acquired as per the very same Notification and the land value fixed by the Land Acquisition Officer is Rs.1,15,200/- per hectare.
7. Initially, the Collector dismissed the Section 28A Applications of the claimant, finding that they were time-barred.
Thereafter, this Court set aside the said Order and directed the Collector to reconsider the Applications.

Thereafter, the Collector passed awards redetermining the land value at the rate of Rs.1000/- per cent with respect to the property in L.A.R. No.26/2015 and redetermining the land value at the rate of Rs.800/- per cent with respect to the property in L.A.R. No.27/2015.

On the request of the claimant, both the cases were referred to the Reference Court and the Reference Court granted enhancement only in LAR No.27/2015, fixing the land value of LA.APP. NO. 238 OF 2019 2025:KER:72256 Rs.1,500/- per cent as the land value fixed at Rs.1,000/- per cent in Ext.A1 was enhanced to Rs.1,500/- as per Ext.A2 judgment of this Court, finding that both the properties are situated in R.S No.309/1.

The reason for denying enhancement in LAR No.26/2015 is that the claimant did not adduce any evidence to show that the acquired property in LAR No.26/2015 and the property covered by Exts.A1 and A2 judgments are comparable.
The approach of the Reference Court is not correct.

When the Land Acquisition Officer has granted the same land value for the acquired property as well as the property covered in Exts.A1 and A2, the Reference Court ought to have relied on Exts.A1 and A2 to fix the land value in LAR No.26/2015.
The Respondents could not contend that both properties are not comparable when they have given the same land value for both properties.
Merely because two properties are situated in the same Survey Number, they could not be treated as having the same importance and value.
For example, one may have road frontage and the other may not have road frontage, which would result in a LA.APP. NO. 238 OF 2019 2025:KER:72256 considerable difference in land value.
When the Land Acquisition Officer has granted the same value for all these properties, the Reference Court should have fixed the land value in LAR Nos.26 and 27 of 2015, relying on the same.

The Reference Court illegally denied the land value of Rs.1,500/- per cent in LAR No.26/2015, which is granted in Ext.A2 and in LAR No.27/2015.
8.
In view of the aforesaid discussion, I am of the view that the appellant/claimant in LAR No.26/2015 is also entitled to get fixation of land value at Rs.1,500/- for 0.3760 hectares acquired from him.
9. Accordingly, this appeal is allowed with proportionate costs, setting aside the impugned judgment in LAR No.26/2015 fixing the land value at Rs.1,500/- per cent for the acquired land.

The claimant is entitled to get all statutory benefits and interest.
Sd/-
M.A.ABDUL
HAKHIM
